newsitem.title: UK: EUROPEAN GASOLINE DROPS $13 AS SQUEEZE ENDS.
newsitem.headline: EUROPEAN GASOLINE DROPS $13 AS SQUEEZE ENDS.

text.p: A $13 a tonne dive in prompt European gasoline prices early on Friday signalled the end of a market squeeze by Wall Street trader Morgan Stanley, London-based brokers said.
The squeeze was seen contributing to a $25 jump in first half August Eurograde gasoline over the past week, brokers said.

"It looks like it's over now. They've not been very keen today, it's all very low profile," one broker said, referring to Morgan Stanley, which had throughout this week been identified as the dominant prompt buyer.
It was Morgan Stanley that was seen buying the $240.25 first half August barge Wednesday, representing the highest recorded price level since the Gulf War.
The gains helped boost refinery margins in Europe to over $3.00 a barrel for running Brent crude oil, a level likely to fall sharply on Friday.

But although a $216 fob ARA deal was done on Friday morning in the absence of Morgan Stanley on the maket, a subsequent deal at $220 indicated to some dealers that the end of the squeeze would not necessarily herald the end of bullish market sentiments.
Some predicted that what they saw as a fundamentally tight physical market would still support prices as second half August approaches.
